title: Nine Candles and One Guest
subtitle: 节日庆典 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 节日庆典（文学艺术与体育·节日与庆典）
meta: 主题语境：节日庆典（文学艺术与体育·节日与庆典）　|　核心词汇：birthday　|　正文 336 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 birthday 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1950 my brother was given ① a birthday with nine candles and one guest, and my mother said the guest was the whole of the party. The ② birthday, meaning the day and not the celebration, fell on a Tuesday and was moved to the Saturday; a birthday, she said, is the only date that everybody agrees to lie about.

Every ③ birthday in that house was celebrated on the wrong day, and the ④ birthday in March, meaning the one that had been moved twice and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever questioned. A birthday, my grandmother said, is nine parts permission and one part a cake somebody has time to make; my mother said the permission is the part that matters.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ birthday was the whole of the year, meaning the age and not the day. The ⑥ birthday, meaning the number you have become and not any of that, is the only thing in a life that arrives once and is carried for twelve months; a birthday, he said, is either something with candles or the only word that means both a day and an age. She said the age is the part they notice.

By 1967 the ⑦ birthday had become a photograph in an album, and the album had become an argument about which year it was. The ⑧ birthday of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine candles and eleven years of moving; a birthday, she said, is either the day in March or the reason you learned which week you were born in. He said the week has never been agreed on.

The ⑨ birthday I remember is the one in March, which was moved twice and is still being argued about. A ⑩ birthday, my grandmother said in 1969, is the only date that improves by being moved; every birthday, she said, is an age that has agreed to look like a day. She said the age was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 生日（指那一天，与庆祝活动相对）
C. 固定搭配：be given a birthday 过／得到一个生日
D. n. 生日（指屋里每一次）
E. n. 生日（指三月那一次）
F. n. 年龄；年岁（指长成的那个数字）
G. n. 年龄（抽象：那个数字这件事）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: The birthday, meaning the day and not the celebration
birthday was the whole of the year
The birthday, meaning the number you have become
the birthday had become a photograph in an album
The birthday of the whole thing
A birthday, my grandmother said in 1969

answers.why: be given a birthday 意为“过／得到一个生日”，1950 年家里给弟弟过了一个有九支蜡烛、只来一位客人的生日。
birthday 意为“生日”，指那一天而不是庆祝活动，它落在星期二，被挪到了星期六。
birthday 指屋里每一次生日，那屋里每一个都是在错的日子过的。
birthday 指三月那一次（被挪过两次的那一个），是唯一有人提出疑问的。
birthday 意为“年龄、年岁”，指长成的那个数字，父亲说 birthday 就是那一年的全部。
birthday 为抽象用法，指那个数字这件事，是一生中唯一来一次、却要被带着走十二个月的东西。
birthday 意为“生日”，到 1967 年这个 birthday 成了相册里的一张照片。
birthday 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九支蜡烛和十一年的挪动。
birthday 意为“生日”，我记得的是三月那一次，它被挪过两次，至今还在被争论。
birthday 为抽象总称，祖母说生日是唯一会因为被挪动而变好的日子。
